Q: Are there security issues with using responseXML property of XMLHttpRequest? A:

the format doesn't really matter as much as what you do with the untrusted data afterwards. In general responseXML should be fairly safe to use in modern browsers since they'll ignore the DTD which is where most XML exploits come from. You need to be careful what you do with the data afterwards especially if populating the DOM with it. Better to sanitize user-input on the way in... (for files, best to run a full virus scan too)

Q: Is it a good or a bad idea to join two tables on several columns if joining on one column is enough? A:

I don't know clickhouse. From the viewpoint of a relational database you would never have this situation, because you wouldn't store data redundantly in order to avoid data inconsistencies (here: have the same event with different user or product, which is not allowed). You would store user_id and product_id in only one table.

And from a data warehouse perspective you might decide to do store the data redundantly (that you'd get from a normalized database), so as to avoid joins, but well, then you wouldn't have to join.

Q: How to chain these two Postman requests A:

To wait 30 sec use setTImeout in prerequest script:

setTimeout(()=>{},30000)

This will wait for 30 seconds

Now to send the id url you can directly add it to url as {{id}} or in prerequest script add :

pm.request.addQueryParams({key:"id",value:pm.variables.get("id")})

if you want to run the request again and again till you get 200:

add this to test section of request 2

if (pm.response.code !== 200) {
    setTimeout(()=>{postman.setNextRequest(pm.info.requestName)},5000)
    

}

Note: there is a automatic delay between request option in postman you can use that also.

Also setNextRequest works only if you run using newman or colection runner

Q: How does one enforce/who should enforce (app developer? library developer?) how multiple C++ libraries should or should NOT be loaded together? A:

It should be the app developer's responsibility to keep track of all dependencies their app requires. In this example, the solution would be for the dev to update app to link to libcore.so.2 to match with the other dependent libraries it is using.

Q: PostgreSQL WHERE created_at <= timestamp slow on large table on (140M rows) A:

I am with Josh here: why would you need to read all these rows? It certainly won't be for a person having to manually read millions of rows. So, it's a process? And it must read again and again all these rows? (If it were a one-time query, lack of speed wouldn't bother you.) Why wouldn't that process know like 99% of the data from the last time it read the data and only request the missing 1%?

All in all, something seems off with the approch. It shouldn't be necessary to read millions of complete rows from the same table again and again. This means, it is probably not the query you want to optimize, but the process.
